subject.title: [Feature]: Built-in auto-update with configurable schedule, confirmation, and post-update notification

question: Should OpenClaw core add a first-class updater workflow beyond the existing package rollout updater, and what approval, scheduling, channel-targeting, and post-restart reporting contract should it expose?
rationale: The remaining work defines new config, consent, unattended package execution, restart persistence, and cross-channel notification behavior, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent product and security boundary.

options.title: Design safe core workflow
options.body: Define the opt-in config, approval modes, notification routing, restart-state persistence, and `update.run` or external-updater execution boundary before implementation.

options.title: Keep package updater only
options.body: Leave `update.auto` as rollout/cadence policy and route confirmation or notification orchestration to user cron, agents, or plugins until stronger core demand is confirmed.

options.title: Split narrower follow-ups
options.body: Track post-update hooks, UI discoverability, safe rollback, skill/plugin auto-update, and external-updater mechanics separately while keeping this issue as the workflow umbrella.

recommendation.title: Design safe core workflow
recommendation.body: Define the opt-in config, approval modes, notification routing, restart-state persistence, and `update.run` or external-updater execution boundary before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the current package auto-updater and authored product-facing review context for the remaining workflow gap.
